name: Sovereign Gold Bond vs Physical Gold Calculator India
seoTitle: SGB vs Physical Gold Calculator India | Net Return
targetKeyword: Sovereign Gold Bond vs physical gold calculator India
shortDescription: Compare an SGB-style holding with physical gold after coupon interest, assumed gold appreciation, making charges and storage costs.
metaDescription: Compare SGB and physical gold returns in India using investment, coupon, gold appreciation, holding period, making charges and storage costs.
formulaExplanation: Compounds both holdings by the same entered gold-price appreciation, adds simple annual SGB interest, and subtracts physical-gold making charges plus storage costs.
example: On Rs 5 lakh held for eight years, making charges and recurring storage costs can create a material gap even before tax treatment is considered.

faqs.question: Does this include tax on SGB interest or gold gains?
faqs.answer: No. Tax depends on the instrument, holding route and rules applicable when you sell or redeem. Entered results are pre-tax educational estimates.

faqs.question: Does the SGB estimate include market-price discounts or premiums?
faqs.answer: No. It assumes the entered investment tracks the chosen gold appreciation rate and does not model secondary-market liquidity or pricing differences.

name: Index Fund vs Active Fund Cost Calculator India
seoTitle: Index vs Active Fund Cost Calculator India
targetKeyword: index fund vs active fund cost calculator India
shortDescription: Compare how two expense ratios change future value when both funds earn the same assumed gross return before costs.
metaDescription: Compare index and active fund expense-ratio drag in India using investment amount, years and the same assumed gross return.
formulaExplanation: Subtracts each expense ratio from the same assumed gross return and compounds both net return assumptions for the selected period.
example: The comparison isolates fee drag only; it does not assume either fund generates better or worse gross performance.

faqs.question: Does a lower expense ratio guarantee a higher return?
faqs.answer: No. This calculator deliberately holds gross return constant to isolate cost drag. Actual fund performance, tracking difference and portfolio choices vary.

faqs.question: Does this include exit load or tax?
faqs.answer: No. It compares recurring expense ratios only and excludes one-time charges, transaction costs and tax.

name: ELSS Lock-in vs Other 80C Options Calculator India
seoTitle: ELSS vs PPF vs Tax-Saver FD Lock-in Calculator
targetKeyword: ELSS lock in vs PPF FD calculator India
shortDescription: Compare illustrative ELSS, tax-saver FD and PPF values at their common statutory lock-in periods and over a shared 15-year horizon.
metaDescription: Compare ELSS, tax-saver FD and PPF values at 3, 5 and 15-year lock-ins, plus a common 15-year horizon.
formulaExplanation: Compounds a single investment at the entered return assumptions for the fixed 3-year ELSS, 5-year tax-saver FD and 15-year PPF lock-ins, then compares all three at 15 years.
example: The native lock-in outputs show when each option first becomes accessible; the 15-year outputs provide a like-for-like compounding horizon.

quickAnswer.title: ELSS, PPF and Tax-Saver FD Lock-ins
quickAnswer.question: How do the Section 80C lock-ins compare?
quickAnswer.answer: ELSS units have a 3-year lock-in, tax-saver bank FDs generally have a 5-year lock-in, and PPF has a 15-year base tenure. Returns, risk, liquidity and tax treatment differ.
quickAnswer.note: Verify current rules and product terms before investing.

links.label: Read the PPF vs ELSS vs FD Section 80C guide

faqs.question: Is ELSS return guaranteed after three years?
faqs.answer: No. ELSS is market-linked, and the 3-year lock-in is not a promised return period. Value can be above or below the investment.

faqs.question: Are these post-tax maturity values?
faqs.answer: No. The calculator compares pre-tax compounding assumptions. Interest and capital-gains treatment can differ across ELSS, PPF and tax-saver FDs.

name: NPS Tier 2 vs Mutual Fund Calculator India
seoTitle: NPS Tier 2 vs Mutual Fund Calculator India
targetKeyword: NPS Tier 2 vs mutual fund calculator India
shortDescription: Compare monthly investing in NPS Tier 2 and an equity mutual fund using return and withdrawal-tax assumptions for each route.
metaDescription: Compare NPS Tier 2 and mutual fund corpus values using monthly contribution, years, expected returns and withdrawal-tax assumptions.

inputs.label: Assumed NPS Tier 2 tax on gains

formulaExplanation: Uses monthly annuity-due compounding for each return assumption, then applies the entered illustrative tax rate only to estimated gains at withdrawal.
example: Changing either expected return or the assumed tax rate can materially alter the post-tax comparison over a long holding period.

faqs.question: Does NPS Tier 2 have the same tax benefit as NPS Tier 1?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. Tier 2 liquidity and tax treatment differ from Tier 1 and can depend on investor category and current rules.

faqs.question: Are the entered tax rates applied to the whole corpus?
faqs.answer: No. This simplified model applies each entered rate only to estimated gains, not to contributed principal.

name: XIRR / Portfolio Return Calculator India
seoTitle: XIRR Portfolio Return Calculator India | Approximation
shortDescription: Approximate an annualised portfolio return for up to three investments using their amounts, years held and current combined value.
metaDescription: Approximate annualised portfolio return in India for up to three lumpsum investments with different holding periods and one current value.
formulaExplanation: Uses an amount-weighted average holding period, then annualises the total portfolio gain as a closed-form CAGR approximation. It is not an iterative date-accurate XIRR solve.
example: Rs 1 lakh held five years, Rs 1.5 lakh held three years and Rs 2.5 lakh held one year have an amount-weighted holding period of 2.4 years.

faqs.question: Is this the same as Excel XIRR?
faqs.answer: No. Excel XIRR iteratively solves dated cash flows. This calculator uses a transparent weighted-holding-period approximation compatible with RupeeKit's single-expression engine.

faqs.question: When should I use a full XIRR calculation instead?
faqs.answer: Use date-accurate XIRR when cash flows are irregular, include withdrawals or dividends, or when precise performance reporting is required.

name: Rule of 72 / Doubling Time Calculator India
seoTitle: Rule of 72 Calculator India | Doubling Time
shortDescription: Estimate how many years an investment may take to double, compare the Rule of 72 with exact annual compounding and view preset rates.
metaDescription: Estimate investment doubling time with the Rule of 72, compare exact annual compounding and see preset results for 8%, 10%, 12% and 15%.
formulaExplanation: Divides 72 by the entered annual return for the common approximation and compares it with log(2) divided by log(1 + return) for exact annual compounding.
example: At 12% a year, the Rule of 72 estimates 6 years to double, while exact annual compounding takes about 6.12 years.

faqs.question: Is the Rule of 72 a guaranteed doubling period?
faqs.answer: No. It is a mental-math approximation. Market-linked returns vary and may be negative in some periods.

faqs.question: When is the Rule of 72 most accurate?
faqs.answer: It is generally closest around moderate annual rates. The exact-compounding output shows how the approximation differs for your entered rate.
